analysis.title: "These Really Matter": Everything You Need To Know Ahead Of Microsoft And Alphabet Earnings
key_insights: Microsoft and Alphabet report after the close on Oct 28, 2026, a few hours after a Fed meeting where a 'hawkish hold' is the consensus. MSFT is the consensus long and GOOGL is described by UBS as 'still feels like the consensus funding short across megacaps.'

After the July prints, GOOGL fell 7% the next day (revenue +24%, Google Cloud +82%, 2026 capex forecast raised to as much as $205B). MSFT rose 16% a week later, its biggest one-day gain since 2008, with capex outlook unchanged and short interest at its highest since 2015. Since then MSFT is up 35%, GOOGL down 5%, Nasdaq 100 up just over 2%.

Goldman's Privorotsky: buyside is closer to Azure growth in the high 40s% and Google Cloud in the mid 90s%. Azure probably needs a guidance raise to be supportive. A miss caused only by compute capacity would hurt near-term revenue but could support the scarcity premium and future spending. Watch customer concentration, and the link between revenue growth, capex and margins.

Hedge funds are the most bearish in five years while the S&P is 1% from a record. Goldman's floor saw about $20B of TMT selling over two weeks, vs $23B during July's AI unwind. The GS Vol Panic Index hit 7.94 on Friday, the first time at the 'panic' bogey since late July.
Global Info Tech stocks saw the largest 2-week % net selling on Goldman Prime's record (Oct 5-16), while Mag 7 net exposure rose to a new record high.

Goldman's derivatives desk has MSFT at 8/10 on its positioning score, the same score Meta carried into its print last week. JPM's Heavey says GOOG is used as a source of funds, with another negative third-party check ahead of earnings pointing to a Search miss. GOOGL fell 10% from its Oct 13 high into Monday.

Options price the event cheaply relative to history. MSFT implied move is 4.7-4.8% vs 15.5% realized last quarter and a 4.6% average realized move. GOOGL straddle is 5.6% vs a 5.2% average realized move. Mag 7 implied vol relative to broad tech is in the 15th percentile vs the last 4 years.

Alphabet buyside bar: Search growth about 14% vs Street about 15% (UBS bogey 14-14.5%). Per JPM's Schilsky, alt data points to roughly a 100 bps Search miss, and a Search beat would likely send the stock higher the next day. YouTube about 11-12%. Google Cloud: buyside +105% to +115% (Schilsky), UBS +100-115%, Goldman analysts about +100%, Goldman desk mid-90s, vs Street +90-96%. Implied TPU sales mostly $5-7B in the quarter.

Bloomberg consensus for Alphabet: Google Cloud revenue median $29.1B (range $24.3B to $36.7B), Search $64.9B, YouTube $11.4B, operating income $43.2B. Capex $55.8B against $53.9B operating cash flow gives negative free cash flow of $3.5B.

Schilsky says Google Cloud margin is the most important number. A beat to the Street's roughly 33% EBIT margin would validate that TPU margins are near or above core Cloud margins. Goldman notes modest cloud margin pressure and that Search still funds the build.

TPU demand news: OpenAI plans to buy Google TPUs, Oracle will offer them on its cloud from 2027, and MediaTek rose as much as 6.6%. Anthropic disclosed plans to spend up to $114.5B with Google through 2033.
UBS says Alphabet sentiment needs a credible AI agent and a broader Gemini 4 rollout. Goldman's Sheridan expects a consumer agent launch possibly with Gemini 4 before the holidays.

Alphabet 2026 capex guide is $195-205B and UBS expects a reiteration. 2027 capex is the key number: Street about $305B, JPM buyside $330-350B, UBS $350-375B, Goldman $350B. A 70%+ jump to $350B or more is now the bull case. 2027 Google Cloud growth is +68% for the Street vs >+100% for most investors.

Deutsche Bank notes the AI divide dates from Oct 29, 2025: since then MSFT is about -2% (roughly flat) and GOOGL is up about 24%. DB says the AI trade probably cracks if mega-cap spending unexpectedly slows or if investors stop believing it earns an adequate return.

Goldman's Borges calls MSFT the cleanest AI setup. Upside case: Azure 46-47% cc vs 44-45% guidance and a fiscal Q2 guide of 46-47%, M365 Commercial Cloud 17-18% cc vs 17% guidance. Street is at 45%. UBS puts the buyside Azure bogey near 47%, about 2 points above the Street.

Buyside asks for MSFT: fiscal Q2 Azure guide of 46-47%, 5-7 million additional Copilot seats q/q (30 million paid M365 Copilot seats as of July), and M365 upside from usage-based pricing and the AI security suite. UBS cites OpenAI revenue, capacity additions, GPU pricing and hosted GPU exposure as the Azure upside drivers.

Bloomberg consensus for MSFT: revenue $90.6B (+17% cc), Azure $32.2B, adjusted EPS $4.72, operating margin 48.3%, capex including finance leases $51.8B (vs $41B last quarter), adjusted FCF $8.5B (10% margin).

Goldman has MSFT fiscal 2028 capex at $319B vs Street $252B. MSFT offered buyouts to 60,000 workers two days ago. MSFT leases signed but not yet commenced were $329.1B in July, up from $196.6B. Goldman's Lynam puts the five hyperscalers' off-balance-sheet leases and purchase commitments at $2.8T, eightfold since 2023, with an update due in tonight's 10-Qs.

Privorotsky's checklist: capex flat or up is fine and a cut would be disastrous for picks-and-shovels names; backlog conversion; FCF conversion; financing mix. Scenarios: worst is capex accelerating on expensive debt or capex cut for lack of financing; best is capex rising with accelerating organic cash flow; middle is flat/up capex with more equity financing, bad for equity and potentially good for credit.

Funding is getting costlier. Meta raised up to $95B from shareholders after turning FCF negative, and Broadcom guaranteed a $63B SPV for Anthropic's TPU purchases. JPM credit says hyperscaler spreads are back at July wides, IG hyperscaler issuance has been largely absent since Google's $25B deal on Aug 6, and all-in funding costs are up about 120 bps. Issuance could return after earnings.

JPM's Heavey reads the AI rally into earnings as pricing a dovish Fed, some geopolitical resolution and a renewed capex upcycle without new funding needs, which he calls a low-probability combination.

Author's view: positioning favors Alphabet on day one (a funding short with an in-line Search print and a TPU-fueled cloud beat could squeeze). Both are expected to clear the cloud bar and say 'higher' on 2027 spending. The two companies combine for roughly $108B of quarterly operating cash flow with nearly $102B going to capex. The author expects funding to be more expensive. Amazon reports Oct 29 and about two-thirds of S&P market cap will have reported by Friday.

market_movers.rationale: Funding short with a Search miss largely priced in. An in-line Search print plus a TPU-driven Cloud beat is described as a squeeze setup. A 2027 capex guide of $350B or more is the bull case.
Consensus long positioned 8/10, up 35% since its last print. Buyside needs Azure near 47% and a raised guide, so a beat alone may not be enough.
MediaTek rose as much as 6.6% in Taipei on news OpenAI plans to buy Google TPUs.

sector_views.rationale: Hedge funds are underweight tech, yet Mag 7 net exposure is at a record. The debate has shifted from cloud growth to capex funding, free cash flow and returns.

earnings_insights: MSFT fiscal Q1 consensus (Bloomberg, estimate): revenue $90.6B (+17% cc), Azure $32.2B, adjusted EPS $4.72, operating margin 48.3%, capex incl. finance leases $51.8B, adjusted FCF $8.5B. Reports after close Oct 28, 2026.

MSFT Azure growth: guidance 44-45% cc, Street estimate 45%, Goldman upside case 46-47% cc, UBS buyside bogey about 47% y/y. Goldman's Borges expects a fiscal Q2 guide of about 46-47% cc. M365 Commercial Cloud estimate 17-18% cc vs 17% guidance.

GOOGL Q3 consensus (Bloomberg, estimate): Google Cloud revenue median $29.1B (range $24.3B to $36.7B), Search $64.9B, YouTube $11.4B, operating income $43.2B, capex $55.8B, operating cash flow $53.9B, free cash flow -$3.5B. Cloud EBIT margin estimate about 33%.

GOOGL growth expectations (estimates): Search Street about 15%, buyside about 14%, UBS bogey 14-14.5%. Google Cloud Street +90-96%, buyside +100-115%. YouTube about 11-12%. Paid clicks grew 13% in Q2 and comps get 3 points harder. Operating income buyside bar about $45B per the text, UBS $44-45B.

Alphabet's July 22 print (reported): revenue +24%, Google Cloud +82%, 2026 capex forecast raised to as much as $205B. The stock fell 7% the next day. Microsoft's late-July print (reported) kept capex outlook unchanged and the stock rose 16%.

2027 estimates for Alphabet: capex Street about $305B, JPM $330-350B, UBS $350-375B, Goldman $350B. EPS $14.50-16.00 per JPM and $15-16 per UBS vs the Street at about $15 (extraction of the garbled equation text is uncertain). 2027 Google Cloud growth Street +68%, most investors >+100%.
Goldman fiscal 2028 MSFT capex estimate $319B vs Street $252B. DB proxy review: Azure growth beat management's internal 34% target by 5.7 points.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A hawkish hold is the consensus for the meeting held a few hours before the MSFT and GOOGL prints.
Reached the bogey for 'panic' for the first time since late July.
JPM credit desk estimate. Higher funding costs raise the cost of the capex build and could limit buybacks or capex.

risk_factors: Capex funded increasingly by expensive debt, or capex cut because financing is unavailable (Goldman's worst cases).
Hyperscaler spreads at July wides, funding costs up about 120 bps, and issuance returning after earnings could add supply pressure.
MSFT's high positioning (8/10), a 35% rally since its last print, and buyside Azure expectations above the Street leave little room for an in-line print.
An Azure miss caused by compute capacity limits would hurt near-term revenue.
A Search miss of roughly 50-100 bps and Cloud margin pressure, which would add to the spending narrative.
Mega-cap capex slowing or investors doubting the return on it could crack the AI trade (Deutsche Bank).
Off-balance-sheet leases and purchase commitments of the five leading hyperscalers total $2.8T, up eightfold since 2023.
OpenAI valuation target trimmed to $1.25T after investor pushback, which may complicate the OpenAI contribution to MSFT bookings.
Power and capital are the key constraints on raw materials for AI (Pasquariello).
vol_and_positioning: Goldman positioning score: MSFT 8/10, the same score Meta carried into its print last week.
MSFT implied move 4.7% (GS Vol Views) or 4.8% (Coppersmith) vs 15.5% realized last quarter and a 4.6% average realized move. GOOGL straddle 5.6% as of Friday vs a 5.2% average realized move.
Mag 7 implied vol is offered cheaply vs the broader tech complex, in the 15th percentile of the last 4 years. MSFT is +50% off its summer lows.

Goldman Vol Panic Index 7.94 on Friday. Goldman Prime: record 2-week net selling of Global Info Tech (Oct 5-16) with Mag 7 net exposure at a record high. Hedge funds are the most bearish in five years. About $20B of TMT selling over two weeks vs $23B in July's AI unwind.

GOOGL is being used as a source of funds (JPM). A buyer of 50k GOOGL 15Jan 360 calls was seen on Tuesday (Goldman US desk). Privorotsky says re-risking has barely begun and the move so far is 'abatement of supply, rather than meaningful fresh demand.'
Investor expectations gauge from JPM: GOOGL 5 out of 10, Meta 9 out of 10 last week.
geopolitical: JPM's Heavey says the AI rally into earnings prices some resolution to geopolitical conflicts, which he considers a low-probability combination alongside a dovish Fed and a capex upcycle with no new funding needs.
cross_bank_references: UBS: Alphabet 'still feels like the consensus funding short across megacaps.'
JPM's Schilsky and UBS bogeys are combined with Goldman's analysts' Search estimate, 1% below consensus.
Goldman's Privorotsky, JPM's Schilsky and UBS all cite buyside Google Cloud growth expectations above the Street.
Goldman's Borges and UBS both see Azure at about 46-47% as the upside case or bogey.
Goldman estimates 2027 Alphabet capex at $350B, in line with JPM's $330-350B and below UBS's $350-375B.

tension_points.bull_case: Google Cloud is expected to crush estimates on TPU sales, with buyside at +105-115% vs Street +90-96%, and Cloud revenue could match Search by late 2028. A funding short with an in-line Search print is a squeeze setup.
tension_points.bear_case: Alt data points to a Search miss of roughly 50-100 bps, paid clicks comps get harder, and Cloud margin pressure plus negative FCF of $3.5B feed the spending narrative.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Search miss of around 100 bps or a Cloud EBIT margin below the Street's ~33%.

tension_points.bull_case: Azure could print 46-47% cc vs 44-45% guidance, with Copilot seat growth and a fiscal Q2 guide of 46-47%.
tension_points.bear_case: MSFT is a consensus long at 8/10 positioning after a 35% rally, and buyside Azure expectations already sit near 47%, so a beat may be priced in. A capacity-limited miss hurts near-term revenue.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Azure below roughly 47% without a raised fiscal Q2 guide, which Goldman says Azure probably needs.

tension_points.bull_case: Capex rises alongside accelerating organic cash flow with a credible path to self-funding through 2027/28, and companies choose equity over debt.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex accelerates on expensive debt, or is cut because financing is unavailable. Spreads are at July wides, funding costs are up about 120 bps, and Meta already turned to equity after FCF went negative.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Capex cut for lack of financing, or 2027 guides that come with materially higher debt-funded spending.

theme_stances.key_argument: The market's verdict will depend on how the hyperscalers pay for higher spending, and the answer is likely more expensively than before.
theme_stances.evidence: these questions that matter far more than another round of headline beats

theme_stances.key_argument: A funding short with an in-line Search print and a TPU-fueled cloud beat is the kind of setup that squeezes.
theme_stances.evidence: the skew probably favors Alphabet tonight

theme_stances.evidence: the cleanest AI setup with Azure upside
